title: SQL injection in product search
description: The q query parameter is concatenated directly into the SQLite LIKE expression. An attacker can change the predicate (and potentially use SQLite UNION expressions) instead of performing a literal search.
evidence: GET /products/search?q=%27%20OR%201%3D1-- returned HTTP 200 with all six products, demonstrating that the supplied quote and predicate altered the query.

title: Stored display name reaches SQL without parameterization in admin review report
description: A customer can set their display_name through PATCH /account. The report endpoint later interpolates that stored value into a quoted SQL WHERE clause, so a malicious display name can alter the query when a staff member requests the report. Use a bound parameter for the author_name comparison.
evidence: PATCH /account accepts arbitrary display_name values up to 60 characters (shopapi/auth.py:116-125), and shopapi/admin.py:77-81 builds the SQL with f"... '{customer['display_name']}' ...". A value containing a quote and SQL expression therefore reaches SQLite in a staff-triggered request.

title: Stored review body is rendered as raw HTML (stored XSS)
description: Review bodies are accepted and stored without HTML sanitization, then rendered using Jinja's safe filter. A reviewer can persist script tags or event-handler markup that executes in every visitor's product-page browser.
evidence: An authenticated POST /products/1/reviews with body '<script>alert(1)</script>' returned 201, and GET /p/MUG-SPECK returned the same script inside <div class="review-body"> without escaping.

title: Unsafe pickle deserialization of client-controlled basket cookie
description: The basket cookie is only base64 encoded and has no signature or integrity protection. read_basket passes attacker-controlled decoded bytes to pickle.loads, allowing a forged cookie containing a pickle gadget to execute arbitrary Python code whenever a basket endpoint reads it.
evidence: shopapi/basket.py:15-23 obtains request.cookies['basket'], base64-decodes it, and calls pickle.loads before any validation; with_basket at lines 26-29 creates the cookie without signing it. The broad exception handler runs only after pickle deserialization and cannot undo gadget execution.

title: Trailing-slash variant bypasses staff-only admin guard
description: The global admin authorization hook compares request.path literally against the set of registered rule strings. The refunds endpoint permits both slash forms (strict_slashes=False), but its registered path is compared as the no-slash form; requesting /admin/refunds/ therefore skips the staff check and reaches the privileged refund handler.
evidence: Unauthenticated POST /admin/refunds/ with {"order_id":1,"amount_pence":1} returned HTTP 200 {"ok":true,"refunded_pence":1}, while GET /admin/users without credentials returned 403. Authorization should be enforced by endpoint identity or a blueprint-wide decorator, not exact path-string matching.
